title: os dev and os start keep their crypto key in two different files, so a secret saved under `npm run dev` reads back as unset under `os start` on the same project database
body:
domain:devx#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbYMkB4dbaYNKufhvBr

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named landing point and a measured repro. Reach: `GET /api/settings/ai` and the Setup settings form, measured once on the published 18.3.0 CLI.
Business reason: "Your First Project" step 6 tells a newcomer to `npm run build` and `npx os start --artifact ./dist/objectstack.json` in the same project they just ran `npm run dev` in. Both commands open the same SQLite file (`.objectstack/data/objectstack.db`), but `os dev` reads the key at `~/.objectstack/dev-crypto-key` and `os start` mints a new one at `<project>/.objectstack/dev-crypto-key`. Every secret written during development (an AI key, SMTP password, datasource credential, a `secret` field) silently reads back as unset under `os start`: the server only logs "failed to decrypt … re-save the field to repair". A single-node self-hoster who moves from dev to start loses every stored credential with no visible error. The comment in `start.ts` (L485, "persisting a key file (~/.objectstack/dev-crypto-key)") shows the intent was one file. Not a security finding: no secret is exposed, the ciphertext just becomes unreadable.
Reader who acts: the triage seat, then a `domain:cli` implementer in `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` (home resolution L187 and the `OS_CRYPTO_AUTOKEY` opt-in at L480–490) and `packages/services/service-settings/src/local-crypto-provider.ts` (`keyFilePath`, L463). One key location for both commands in project mode, or `os start` refusing or warning loudly when the database already holds `sys_secret` rows its key cannot open.
Duplicate search (incl. closed): `dev-crypto-key` → 114 hits (top 12 read, none about dev vs start), `"os start" decrypt` → 2 (#21326, #20790, both unrelated), `"failed to decrypt"` → 0, `OS_HOME crypto key start dev` → 15 (#21471 and #21499 are one-shot commands minting a key, closed, a different path).

QA-source: post-release 18.3.0 newcomer walkthrough, path 1 "Your First Project", anchor #27377

## Reproduction (published @objectstack/cli 18.3.0, Node 22.23.4, npm 10.9.9, empty `HOME`)
1. `npm create objectstack@latest my-app && cd my-app && npm run dev`. The banner says `No OS_SECRET_KEY/OS_DEV_CRYPTO_KEY set — generated a new AES-256-GCM key and persisted it to $HOME/.objectstack/dev-crypto-key`.
2. Sign in as `admin@objectos.ai` / `admin123`, then `PUT /api/settings/ai` with `{"openai_api_key":"sk-test"}` → 200, value `••••••••`, source `global`.
3. Stop dev. `npm run build && npx os start --artifact ./dist/objectstack.json --port 8080`. The banner says `minted a new AES-256-GCM key and persisted it to <project>/.objectstack/dev-crypto-key`; the two key files differ (`cmp`).
4. Sign in again, `GET /api/settings/ai`.

Observed: `openai_api_key` is `{"value": null, "source": "default"}` and the server logs `[SettingsService] failed to decrypt ai.openai_api_key: Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data. Returning null …`. The Setup form shows the key as empty.

Expected: the same project reads its own secrets back under `os start`, or `os start` refuses to boot over a database whose secrets its key cannot open and says which key file the data was written with.
